title: ～がる / ～がっている — showing signs of a feeling (third person)
summary: Added to the stem of an i-adjective or na-adjective of feeling (ほしい, 怖い, 暑い, いやだ), it turns the adjective into a verb meaning “shows signs of feeling ～.” It is used for other people's feelings, not your own.

patterns.form: い形容詞の語幹 ＋ がる（がっている）
patterns.gloss: Drop い from the adjective: ほしい → ほしがる, 怖い → 怖がる, 暑い → 暑がる

patterns.form: な形容詞の語幹 ＋ がる（がっている）
patterns.gloss: Use the stem as it is: いや → いやがる, 不思議 → 不思議がる

body.p: Feeling adjectives such as ほしい and 怖い describe a feeling that only the speaker can really know. To talk about someone else's feeling, add がる to the stem to make a verb. ～がっている shows that the person is in that state now.

You can say 私はほしい (I want it), but for a third person you normally say 彼はほしがっている (he wants it), not 彼はほしい. It describes what you can see from the outside, so it carries a feeling close to “he seems to ～.”
The thing wanted or feared usually takes を instead of が once the word becomes ～がる (おもちゃをほしがる, 犬を怖がる). Do not use it for your own feelings.

examples.ja: 子（こ）どもが新（あたら）しいおもちゃをほしがっています。
examples.romaji: Kodomo ga atarashii omocha o hoshigatte imasu.
examples.tr: The child wants the new toy.
examples.note: ほしい → ほしがる. The object takes を.

examples.ja: 妹（いもうと）は大（おお）きな犬（いぬ）を怖（こわ）がっている。
examples.romaji: Imōto wa ōkina inu o kowagatte iru.
examples.tr: My little sister is afraid of the big dog.
examples.note: 怖い → 怖がる: drop い, add がる.

examples.ja: みんなが暑（あつ）がっているので、窓（まど）を開（あ）けた。
examples.romaji: Minna ga atsugatte iru node, mado o aketa.
examples.tr: Everyone seemed hot, so I opened the window.

pitfalls: Do not use it for yourself. Say 私はほしい, not 私はほしがっている.
～がっている describes outward behavior, so it does not fit the speaker's own emotions.
